title: The Maha Kumbh 2025 Sangam Stampede
dek: Uttar Pradesh promised the 'best-ever managed' Maha Kumbh for the roughly 400 million pilgrims expected in Prayagraj. In the early hours of Mauni Amavasya, a barricade collapse under crowd pressure at the Sangam killed dozens — with the state's official death toll disputed by independent investigations reporting far higher numbers.

heroStat.label: reported death toll range: official figures cite around 30, while a BBC investigation identified evidence of at least 82 deaths

promise.quote: This will be the most well-organised and best-managed Kumbh in history, with foolproof crowd management arrangements for the safety of every pilgrim.
promise.context: Statements made in the lead-up to the 2025 Maha Kumbh Mela at Prayagraj, a 45-day Hindu festival the state government said would draw over 400 million pilgrims, billed as an unprecedented feat of crowd management and infrastructure.

target.description: Safe crowd management at the Sangam and other bathing ghats, particularly on the most auspicious bathing dates when the largest crowds were expected, with no loss of life from crowd-control failures.
target.standard: The state government's own stated 'foolproof' safety commitments and its extensive published crowd-management plan for the mela.

reality.description: In the pre-dawn hours of January 29, 2025 — Mauni Amavasya, the most auspicious bathing day — barricades gave way under pressure from a crowd of an estimated one to two million people converging on the Sangam for the Amrit Snan, triggering a crush. Uttar Pradesh police put the official death toll at 30, with 60 injured, and the state announced ex gratia payments of ₹25 lakh per deceased family alongside a judicial inquiry ordered by Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. Independent reporting disputed the official count: a sting operation by the 4PM news network put the toll at 58, and a BBC investigation identified evidence of at least 82 deaths — figures the state government has not accepted.

gap.metricLabel: Official death toll vs. independently investigated death toll
gap.note: The state government disputes the higher independent figures; this entry reports both rather than treating either as conclusively correct, and flags the discrepancy as unresolved.

money.releasedLabel: Ex gratia compensation announced per deceased family (lakh)
money.notes: This figure reflects only the announced per-family ex gratia compensation based on the state's official death toll of 30; it does not reflect any compensation that may or may not have been paid to families in cases outside the officially acknowledged toll.

timeline.label: 'Best-ever' Kumbh promised
timeline.detail: Uttar Pradesh's government promotes the 2025 Maha Kumbh as the largest and best-managed gathering of its kind in history, expecting over 400 million pilgrims over 45 days.

timeline.label: Stampede at Sangam
timeline.detail: Barricades collapse under crowd pressure during the pre-dawn Amrit Snan on Mauni Amavasya; a crush kills dozens and injures dozens more.

timeline.label: Official toll and inquiry announced
timeline.detail: UP Police confirm 30 dead and 60 injured; Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath orders a judicial inquiry and announces ₹25 lakh ex gratia per deceased family.

timeline.label: Independent tolls dispute official count
timeline.detail: A 4PM news network sting and a separate BBC investigation report substantially higher death tolls (58 and at least 82 respectively) than the official figure of 30.

legalStatus.summary: This is a stub entry. A state judicial inquiry was ordered into the stampede; this entry has not yet traced whether that inquiry's findings have been published or whether any officials have faced accountability for crowd-management failures.

verdict.summary: Preliminary verdict, pending fuller research: a real and serious crowd-safety failure occurred despite extensive advance publicity about 'foolproof' arrangements, and there is a significant, unresolved discrepancy between the government's official death toll and figures reported by independent investigations.
verdict.reasoning: The core facts of the stampede are well corroborated, but this entry has not been able to verify which death-toll figure is more accurate, nor has it traced the outcome of the state's judicial inquiry, which was not public in the sources reviewed.

incomplete: The state judicial inquiry's final findings and any recommendations have not been located or incorporated into this entry.
This entry has not reconciled the wide range of reported death tolls (30 to 82, with figures like 37 and 58 also cited in different reports) into a single confident figure.
Whether any officials responsible for crowd-control planning faced disciplinary or legal consequences has not been established here.
